result.title: Doc-to-LoRA Analysis: Query Conditioning, Wrong Facts, and Distractor Interference
result.comment: 18 pages total: 11 pages including references, plus a 7-page appendix. 5 figures
result.summary: Doc-to-LoRA (D2L) compiles documents into low-rank adapters, allowing language models to use their contents without repeatedly processing the original text. We investigate its suitability for internalizing user memories through factual question answering, controlled interventions, and a production MidBrain memory pipeline. Across Gemma-2-2B and Qwen3-4B, D2L loses accuracy relative to in-context learning, with additional documents introducing substantial interference. Single-document errors frequently match answers to other questions about the same passage, suggesting unreliable question-answer attribution. Layer-wise interventions show that interference accumulates across depth, with more concentrated early damage at larger bank sizes on Gemma. With eight documents, applying the full bank in the initial layers gives similar accuracy to withholding all document contributions there. Source membership is detectable in intermediate states, but trained readers do not reliably resolve the interference. On PersonaMem-v2, joint compilation and normalized adapter composition achieve accuracy close to consolidated text memory when retrieved episodes remain text, but the resulting token savings are modest. Measured throughput gains also depend on model and batch size despite substantial reductions in analytical compute. Together, these findings limit the practical case for D2L as a replacement for text-based memory and motivate investigating online-learning methods that acquire personalized behavior from interactions in which memory is used.

AI.brief_summary: 论文对 Doc-to-LoRA 做诊断性分析：把文档编译成低秩适配器后，用事实问答、受控干预与真实记忆流程检验它能否替代上下文文本处理，发现精度低于 in-context learning、多文档干扰随深度累积、问答归属不可靠，且实际加速有限。
AI.relevance_reason: 其逐层干预、适配器组合与中间状态探针可供核查 LVR 中内部证据是否被真正使用、来源可解码却不被采纳及证据干扰问题；虽为纯文本记忆场景，这套诊断范式可能迁移到视觉证据的 latent 状态分析。
